externally_applied_units.exact_statement_in_translation: On a refined G-tropical space, CPsh is the smallest subsheaf of the continuous real functions containing smooth u with DD u>=0 and stable under uniform limits on every open set. For each ordinal alpha, start with smooth positive-Hessian functions; at a successor take local uniform limits of the previous sheaf, and at a limit take functions locally in an earlier stage. This increasing family equals CPsh for sufficiently large alpha.

externally_applied_units.units: CLD 8.5.1, 8.5.3, 8.5.5; 8.7.1 and 8.7.4; 8.8.4-5; the full supplied excerpt was read
exact_statements_in_translation: Standing hypothesis of 8.5: X is a tropical space of level n without boundary. Lemma 8.5.1: if positive currents T_n converge to T and continuous functions u_n converge locally uniformly to u, then u_n T_n converge to u T.
Lemma 8.5.3: if S is a closed symmetric current of bidegree (p,p), q<=p-1 and alpha is a smooth symmetric (q,q) form, then DD(alpha wedge S)=(DD alpha) wedge S.
Lemma 8.5.5: for a positive closed current T and a continuous psh u, DD(u T) is positive and closed.

Construction 8.7.1: iterating DD(u T) for continuous psh factors produces positive closed currents; these are DD-exact when at least one factor is present. With a Bedford-Taylor base current the construction depends on the Hessian currents. The base delta_X is Bedford-Taylor by Example 8.6.4.
Proposition 8.7.4: for positive closed T, continuous psh u_1,...,u_m and every permutation, the iterated products of their Hessians with T agree in the permuted order.

8.8.4 defines local dpsh functions as the real vector sheaf generated by continuous psh functions and includes smooth functions. 8.8.5 extends multiplication by a continuous u_0 and the iterated Hessian product uniquely by multilinearity in dpsh factors, symmetrically in the Hessian factors. If u_0 is dpsh, DD(u_0 DD u_1 wedge ... wedge DD u_p wedge T)=DD u_0 wedge DD u_1 wedge ... wedge DD u_p wedge T. Smooth DD-null changes in any potential leave the product unchanged even without a Bedford-Taylor base. The source display suppresses T in part of its notation; the application here is the recursively defined products with the integration base delta_X.
externally_applied_units.immediate_proof: 8.5.1 proves multiplication continuity by positive-current estimates and a smooth uniformly close approximation. 8.5.3 tests the derivative and cancels an antisymmetric form against a symmetric closed current. 8.5.5 uses a uniformly closed sheaf containing smooth positive-Hessian generators. 8.7.1 is the recursive construction, not a separate omitted proof. 8.7.4 first fixes one factor, proves interchange with a smooth factor, and applies uniform sheaf closure, then uses adjacent transpositions. 8.8.5 states its multilinear extension and derivative identity by construction; it has no additional separate immediate proof in this source unit.
externally_applied_units.application_check: Local rho+a is actual continuous psh and rho is smooth psh, so a is locally dpsh. Reference changes are smooth DD-null. This gives global mixed currents and DD(a theta_b)=(theta_a-theta) wedge theta_b. Evaluating globally exact top currents on the compact smooth test 1 proves equal mass two. It proves the constant-shift energy identity without nonsmooth Green, concavity, or generated-operator canonicity.

externally_applied_units.exact_statement_in_translation: Let X be a tropical space of level n that is locally differentially separated. Every positive Radon measure induces by restriction to compactly supported smooth functions a positive order-zero current. This map is a continuous bijection from positive Radon measures onto positive currents of bidimension (0,0).
externally_applied_units.immediate_proof: The Radon bound gives continuity on each fixed compact. Injectivity follows from smooth density. For surjectivity a smooth positive cutoff equal to one near a fixed compact bounds the positive functional by its uniform norm; density extends it uniquely to a positive functional on compactly supported continuous functions, hence a Radon measure.
externally_applied_units.application_check: The actual carrier is locally differentially separated by the interior portion of the immediate 15.7.1 proof. Bounded products are positive top currents, hence finite positive Radon measures on compact X. Continuous bounded a therefore has finite integrals in the cubic energy.
externally_applied_units.deeper_unresolved_dependencies: The topological positive-functional/Radon representation step and the density chain's Appendix A foundations are not recursively audited.

exact_applied_statements_in_translation: 6.2.4: on a locally differentially separated refined G-tropical space, for compact K and open neighbourhood U of K there is a smooth function equal to one near K with compact support contained in U.

6.2.5: under local differential separation, a real continuous compactly supported f with support in an open U and a<=f<=b admits, for every positive epsilon, a smooth g with compact support in U, |f-g|<epsilon everywhere and a<=g<=b.

6.2.6: compactly supported smooth functions are dense in compactly supported continuous functions for the inductive limit of uniform topologies at fixed compact supports, and dense in continuous functions for convergence uniformly on compact sets.
